questions.question: Match each Stranger Things number in Column A to its matching converted computer value in Column B.
questions.hint: 11 in binary is 8+2+1 = 1011₂. 9 in binary is 8+1 = 1001₂. 1983 in hex is 7BF₁₆.

questions.subHeader: CONNECTION 02 · GATES OF THE UPSIDE DOWN
questions.question: Match each Hawkins operational situation to the logic gate that governs its exact behavior.
questions.hint: Exclusive choice is XOR; inversion is NOT; simultaneous required conditions is AND.

questions.question: Match each town scenario to the computer science data structure it mirrors.
questions.hint: Last-in First-out is Stack; First-in First-out is Queue; Networks of arbitrary connections are Graphs.

questions.question: Match each Hawkins threat vector to the cyber attack classification it exemplifies.
questions.hint: A puppet army is a Botnet; resource starvation via swarms is DDoS; deceptive camouflage is a Trojan.

questions.question: Treat Hawkins history as a Git repository. Match each event to its corresponding Git operation.
questions.hint: Divergent timeline is a branch; combining is merge; recording snapshot is commit; safe undo is revert.

questions.question: Match each investigative search strategy used by Hawkins residents to its fundamental algorithm.
questions.hint: Step-by-step is Linear; halving sorted items is Binary; going deep is DFS; expanding ripples is BFS.

questions.subHeader: CONNECTION 07 · HOW FAST IS HAWKINS? (TIME COMPLEXITY)
questions.question: Match each Hawkins computation or operational task to its asymptotic Big-O time complexity.
questions.hint: Instant top-stack access is O(1); scanning list is O(n); divide-and-conquer sort is O(n log n); pairwise pairs is O(n²).

questions.question: Match each Hawkins scenario to the Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) pillar it demonstrates.
questions.hint: Extending a parent is Inheritance; one method with different forms is Polymorphism; hiding internals is Abstraction.

questions.question: Match each situation among the Hawkins kids to the operating system concurrency concept it exhibits.
questions.hint: Time slice rotation is Round Robin; circular mutual blocking is Deadlock; single access lock is Mutex.

questions.question: Match Dustin's expedition equipment items to their counterparts in a computer's memory hierarchy.
questions.hint: Fastest in-hand is Register; fast buffer is Cache; active temporary is RAM; bulk persistent is Hard Disk.

options.text: A → L → G → O → R → I → T → H → M (ALGORITHM)
M → O → R → T → A → L → I → G → H (MORTALIGH)
T → E → L → E → G → R → A → M → S (TELEGRAMS)

questions.hint: Unscramble TLHIGROMA: It begins with A and defines every automated program.

questions.question: Unscramble the letters describing the core programming technique where a function calls itself repeatedly until reaching a base condition.

options.text: R → E → C → U → R → S → I → O → N (RECURSION)
C → Uursion → R → E → S → O → N (CURSIONER)
S → U → C → C → E → S → S → I → O (SUCCESSION)
R → E → S → O → U → R → C → I → N (RESOURCING)

questions.hint: Unscramble ECROSNIRU: Like two mirrors facing each other in the Upside Down.

questions.question: Arrange these SQL clauses in correct execution sequence to fetch names of characters with power above 5, sorted alphabetically.

options.text: SELECT name → FROM characters → WHERE power > 5 → ORDER BY name;
FROM characters → SELECT name → ORDER BY name; → WHERE power > 5
WHERE power > 5 → SELECT name → FROM characters → ORDER BY name;
ORDER BY name; → SELECT name → FROM characters → WHERE power > 5

questions.question: The lines of this recursive factorial calculation function are jumbled. Arrange them in valid working order. (What does factorial(5) return?)
questions.hint: Function definition first (B), then base case condition (C) and base return (D), followed by recursive step (A).

questions.question: Rearrange the lines to build a string-reversing function. (Calling it with 'NWOD' reveals a crucial Upside Down clue!)

options.text: B → D → C → E → A (reverse('NWOD') reveals 'DOWN')

questions.subHeader: REARRANGE 07 · SCRAMBLED CODE (SUM OF EVEN NUMBERS)
questions.question: Arrange the lines so the script calculates the sum of all even numbers from 1 to 10. What is the printed output?
questions.hint: Initialize accumulator B, iterate range E, check modulo A, accumulate D, print total C. 2+4+6+8+10 = 30.

questions.question: Arrange the jumbled HTML tags to form a valid document displaying heading 'Hawkins Lab'.

options.text: B → C → E → A → D (Mismatched tags)
E → C → B → D → A (Invalid root)
C → E → B → D → A (Heading outside body)

questions.hint: Document root <html> opens first, then <body>, content inside, then </body> and </html> close.

questions.question: Put the professional Git workflow for creating a feature branch, committing fixes, and pushing in correct chronological order.

options.text: C → E → B → D → A (Clone → Branch → Stage → Commit → Push)
C → B → D → E → A (Commit on main before branch)
E → C → B → D → A (Branch before clone failure)
B → D → A → C → E (Push uninitialized repo)

questions.hint: First clone repo (C), make branch (E), stage modifications (B), commit message (D), push upstream (A).

questions.question: Arrange the chronological steps of a secure client-server user authentication protocol.

options.text: B → D → C → A → E (Submit → Transmit → Verify Hash → Issue Token → Access Granted)
D → B → C → A → E (Transmission before input)
B → C → D → A → E (Client-side database comparison)
A → B → D → C → E (Token generation before authentication)

questions.hint: User inputs (B), browser posts (D), backend hashes and checks (C), server issues token (A), client navigates (E).

The 'total' variable should be initialized to -1

Python requires while loops for array traversal

questions.question: Why does this recursive function crash the Hawkins Lab simulation console with a RecursionError?

Python cannot perform multiplication inside a return statement
The function parameter name must be uppercase
The function needs an external global variable

questions.hint: Without a base condition (like if n <= 1: return 1), fact(n) recurses forever until stack overflow.
